# Fixed: Match imported files whose artist tag lists several artists or holds a web address

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on `feat/artist-alias-distance` and merges after it. Reviewed in [#56](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/56).

Import identification scores the files' artist tag, the album artist where there is one, as a single name against the release artist. Artist is weighted 3.0 in the album distance, as heavily as the album title and below only a tagged release id (5.0). A tag that names the album artist alongside others, such as "Artist A;Artist B" or "Artist A feat. Artist B", took a large artist penalty. A web address that a download site wrote into the album artist tag took the full penalty. Either could leave a correct release short of the import threshold.

- The tag's whole text is scored against the artist's name and aliases as before. A tag that credits several artists, split at `;`, `/`, `,` and `&`, is also scored artist by artist, and the closest one counts with a fixed penalty of 0.2 on top. So a release by one of them only outranks the release credited to all of them when the whole credit misses by more than 0.2. The whole credit is also scored loosely, with "&" read as "and" and a leading "The" dropped on both sides, and the lower score counts: for short names those differences cost more than 0.2, so "A & B" still ranks "The A & B" above "A". The loose reading carries 0.01, so the credit as written still ranks ahead of a different artist spelled the loose way. These readings make a correct release score worse than before only for a tag that leaves out the artist's leading "The", which now costs the loose reading's 0.01 instead of nothing; otherwise the release gains whenever the whole tag missed by more than that penalty. An artist tag longer than 1,000 characters is scored by its first 1,000, since the credit patterns slow down sharply on longer input.
- Guests after "feat.", "ft." or "featuring" are left out, whether a space, a bracket or a list separator comes before them, so "Artist A feat. Artist B", "Artist A;feat. Artist B" and "Artist A (feat. Artist B & Artist C)" count toward Artist A only. The credit without its guests is also scored whole, with 0.01 on top, so a name that contains a separator, such as "Earth, Wind & Fire feat. The Emotions", isn't only scored piece by piece, where "Earth" would match another band. A piece that cleans to nothing, such as "...", isn't scored. A bracketed guest ends at its bracket, so "Artist A (feat. Artist B) & Artist C" still credits Artist C. A guest has to start with a word after the dot or space, so a name that ends in "Feat", alone or followed by ";", "/" or ",", is left whole.
- A credit in another order than the release's, "Artist B & Artist A" against "Artist A & Artist B", still ranks one of its artists first, as on `develop`.
- An artist tag that is entirely a web address (a scheme such as `https://`, a `www.` prefix, or a single word ending in `.com`, `.net`, `.org`, `.info`, `.biz`, `.ru` or `.io`, optionally with a path) isn't scored, as for Various Artists releases, unless the artist's name is itself a web address; then the tag is scored as before. An alias doesn't count here: another artist's release would skip the tag, so an artist with a web-like alias would score worse for it. An address can't contain `;` or `,`, nor `&` outside a query string such as `?a=1&b=2`, so "www.example.com;Artist A" is scored as a list. A name followed by an address, or a dotted name like "d.j.name", is scored as before.
- `Distance.AddStringToClosest` from `feat/artist-alias-distance` becomes `Distance.ClosestPenalty`, which returns the penalty so the two scores can be compared.
- As `feat/artist-alias-distance` now does, the artist's own name is scored ahead of its aliases, for the whole credit and for each credited artist: an alias match costs `Distance.AliasPenalty` (0.05) more, so a tribute act that has the bare name as an alias doesn't beat the real artist. Aliases that clean to nothing are ignored, so files without an artist tag keep the full penalty, and they aren't counted as named like a web address.

Tests: a tag crediting several artists scores closer than the same text as one name, and closer than an unrelated artist; the whole credit outranks one of its artists, including "&" against "and", a missing "The" (also for short names) and a listed name ending in "Feat"; the credit as written outranks its "and" spelling; a name written without its "&" still matches; the main artist outranks a featured guest, bracketed or not, a guest after a list separator is left out, and a co-artist after a bracketed guest still counts; names that contain a separator match themselves; a list naming neither artist, an empty tag and dotted names are still penalised; web addresses, padded, with a path or with a query string, aren't scored unless the artist is named like one, and a name followed by one, or listed with one, still is, also after a query string. Nineteen mutations each fail a test, among them a penalty of 0.1 on a listed artist, guests kept, a bracketed guest running to the end, a guest recognised only after a space, all three earlier guest patterns, the earlier address checks, skipping an address even for an artist named like one, an address with a query string not recognised, no leading-"The" reading, no tie-break on the loose reading, and scoring the whole credit only as written or only loosely; the alias tests still pass.
